html:
The Port of Singapore opened its first container terminal at Tanjong Pagar in 1972, and became one of the busiest container ports in the world. It handles a large share of the goods that pass through the Strait of Malacca.

Singapore had been a free port since its founding in 1819, and the trade of the Straits Settlements passed through it. After independence, betting early on containers kept it ahead of rivals.

The port, together with refining, shipbuilding and finance, made the city-state one of the richest places in Asia. Its terminals are now being moved to a single megaport at Tuas in the west. See also Strait of Malacca.
